## Rule set

Paste the JSON generated by Request Control below. Review it before submitting and remove private/personal URLs, tokens, identifiers, or other sensitive values.

```json

```

## Purpose

Describe what the rule set does and why it is useful.

## Authorship and provenance

State where the submitted rule data came from. This is provenance collection, not an automatic license grant or approval.

- Original work by submitter: `yes` / `no` / `mixed`
- Third-party project/source, if any:
- Immutable source URL or revision, if available:
- Governing license for third-party material, if known:
- Which specific rules/fields are derived or adapted from that source:

Do not describe third-party material as your own. If the source/license is uncertain, say so explicitly so maintainers can keep the submission review-only until the rights/provenance question is resolved. See `docs/licensing-provenance-inventory.md` and issue #13 for the current catalog-licensing review.

## Catalog classification

Suggest the user-facing classification for review. Maintainers may adjust it before publication.

- Presentation: `standard` / `advanced`
- Behavior: direct-link / media-quality / media-url-cleanup / site-cleanup / request-blocking / url-cleanup / privacy-embed / provider-override / special-mode / url-normalization
- Scope: `site-specific` / `cross-site` / `global`
- Risk: `low` / `medium` / `high`

## Example URLs / expected behavior

Provide representative examples that reviewers can use to validate the rules.

## Compatibility notes

List sites or workflows that may require exceptions.

## Checklist

- [ ] I reviewed the JSON and removed private or sensitive information.
- [ ] I identified whether the submission is original, derived/adapted from third-party material, or mixed.
- [ ] I disclosed known third-party source/revision/license information instead of assuming repository publication changes that source license.
- [ ] Rules have stable UUIDs.
- [ ] I included examples for broad rules.
- [ ] I proposed presentation, behavior, scope, and risk metadata.
- [ ] I understand that publication requires review; popularity/reactions are not a safety signal.
